one_liner: Apify has a broad REST API with API-token auth, webhooks, an OpenAPI spec and an official hosted MCP server (OAuth or token); free-plan access comes from draft evidence the fetched pages didn't confirm, so it is likely ready to build.
auth_notes: REST API uses a secret API token as a Bearer header (recommended) or token query param. Apify's integration docs mention OAuth 2.0 for integrations, and the hosted MCP server supports OAuth. The pages show no self-serve OAuth app registration for the main REST API, so API token stays primary.
access_notes: The draft cites a permanent free plan with $5 monthly credit and no card. The fetched pages did not repeat this. They do show that anyone can create an API token on the Console Integrations page, and the MCP README says users without an account can create a free one. Kept from the draft with lower confidence.
blocker_notes: No blocker is visible in the pages. Free credit limits are not a blocker.

evidence.quote: Add the token to your request's `Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>`.
*OAuth 2.0* - Use OAuth 2.0 to allow users to authorize your integration without sharing their credentials.
The hosted endpoint is https://mcp.apify.com . If your client can't use OAuth, send your Apify API token in an Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN> header instead.
**You can create an API token on the [Integrations](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations) page in the Apify Console.**
If you don't have an account, you can create a free one there.
The API is organized around [RESTful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer) HTTP endpoints.
The official Apify Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives AI agents web scraping, data extraction, and browser automation
